en.p: In the coordinate plane there are a circle $C$ centered at the origin with radius 2 and two points $\mathrm{A}(2,\,0)$, $\mathrm{B}(0,\,-2)$. For a point P on circle $C$ with negative $x$-coordinate, let $\angle\mathrm{PAB}=\theta$. Let R be the foot of the perpendicular from the point $\mathrm{Q}(0,\,2\cos\theta)$ to the line BP, and let $f(\theta)$ be the distance between the two points P and R. What is the value of $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}f(\theta)\,d\theta$? [4 points]
